builder_plan.scenario: An agent looks good in demos, but you cannot tell which product tasks it fails.
builder_plan.change: Use the study's evaluation idea to inspect a small set of tasks with human-checked answers.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current evaluator and a manually reviewed reference set.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Agreement with human review, missed failures, false alarms, and evaluation cost per task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: EgoUseBench: Benchmarking Computer-Use Agents under Evolving First-Person Contexts
summary: EgoUseBench replaces ad hoc testing of computer-use agents with a structured benchmark of 693 tasks built from 74+ hours of first-person recordings, covering static instructions, prerecorded egocentric context, and continuously evolving observations. Adoption costs the engineering effort of integrating egocentric video streams and evolving task state into an evaluation harness, which is nontrivial on a constrained setup and irrelevant if the reader's agents do not consume wearable sensor input. It can fail as a proxy if the reader's production tasks differ from the benchmark's web-task distribution, and the reported 26.3-point Online Ego Use gap indicates current models handle this setting poorly, so strong benchmark scores elsewhere should not be extrapolated to egocentric deployment.
rationale: This is an evaluation benchmark, not a deployable technique, so it offers no production gain unless the reader is building agents grounded in first-person wearable context.
technique: Benchmark for agents with egocentric context

Adoption costs the engineering effort of integrating egocentric video streams and evolving task state into an evaluation harness, which is nontrivial on a constrained setup and irrelevant if the reader's agents do not consume wearable sensor input. It can fail as a proxy if the reader's production tasks differ from the benchmark's web-task distribution, and the reported 26.3-point Online Ego Use gap indicates current models handle this setting poorly, so strong benchmark scores elsewhere should not be extrapolated to egocentric deployment.

No improvement claim; the paper reports that evaluated agents score on average 26.3 percentage points lower in Online Ego Use than in standard Computer-Use settings, indicating a capability gap rather than a gain.
